title: Tools: diagrams as code (Mermaid, PlantUML, Structurizr)

videos.script: Every diagram in this course so far was a picture. Pictures have a problem. You cannot see what changed between two versions of one. {{title}} A diagram written as text can be reviewed like code. A pull request shows the arrow that was added and the box that was renamed. {{diff}} This lesson installs three tools that turn text into diagrams. Mermaid, which GitHub draws on its own. PlantUML, which knows every UML diagram. And Structurizr, which keeps one model and draws every C4 view from it. {{tools}} It is also the only lesson in this course where you type commands. So it starts with your lab. Three ways to set it up, what each costs your computer, and what to do when it fails. {{lab}} And it ends where text pays off most. A pipeline that refuses a broken diagram before anybody sees it. {{pipeline}}
